title: Galbitang
subtitle: Clear beef short rib soup
excerpt: Bone-in beef short ribs are blanched, then simmered low and slow for two hours in a clean broth with Korean radish, garlic and ginger until the meat is falling-soft and the stock has turned silky. This recipe serves 4 and is a dish that rewards patience. It is one of Korea's most respected soups, served at celebrations and as a restorative meal.
sourceNotes: Galbitang has been a prestige dish in Korean cuisine for hundreds of years, associated with celebrations, ancestral rites and special occasions. The long cooking time and use of short ribs on the bone made it a dish for days when effort and respect were being shown. Today it is cooked at home on weekends when there is time to let it simmer slowly.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the broth and meat in portions for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently. Add fresh spring onions and garnish when serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a larger pot and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Skim the solidified fat from the surface before reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the soup a day ahead and refrigerate. The fat rises and solidifies overnight and can be skimmed cleanly before reheating, giving a cleaner final broth.

glossaryTerms.definition: Tang is the Korean word for a clear broth-based soup, typically made by simmering meat, bones and vegetables over a long period. Tang soups are distinguished from jjigae (thicker stews) by their lighter consistency and clear appearance. They are usually seasoned simply to allow the natural flavour of the main ingredient to come through.

Galbi refers to beef or pork short ribs in Korean cooking. The word means 'rib' and the cut is used in two main applications: galbi gui (grilled marinated ribs) and galbitang (clear rib soup). For soup, the ribs are kept bone-in so the collagen in the bone marrow enriches the broth during the long simmering process.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes around 2 hours 20 minutes in total.

The blanching step is not optional. Covering the ribs with cold water, bringing to the boil, draining and rinsing them removes blood and impurities that would otherwise cloud the broth and give it a bitter edge. A clear galbitang starts with properly blanched ribs.

items.prepNote: bone-in pieces, cut into individual ribs
soaked in cold water for 20 minutes, optional

content.text: Place the short ribs in a large saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to the boil over a high heat and boil for 5 minutes. Drain, then rinse the ribs thoroughly under cold running water to remove any impurities. Clean the pan.
Return the cleaned ribs to the pan with the 2 litres of fresh water. Add the garlic, ginger and the 2 whole spring onions. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Simmer with the lid partially on for 1 hour, skimming any foam or fat from the surface every 20 minutes.
Remove and discard the whole spring onions and ginger. Add the radish and soy sauce. Continue to simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until the radish is tender and the broth has a clean, clear golden colour.
If using glass noodles, add the soaked noodles in the final 5 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt to taste. Finish with a few drops of sesame oil. Ladle into bowls, making sure each person gets at least one rib and some radish. Garnish with the sliced spring onions.

items.symptom: Broth is cloudy and grey rather than clear and golden
items.cause: The ribs were not blanched properly, or the soup boiled too hard during simmering
items.fix: Always blanch the ribs in a separate batch of cold water and rinse them before the main simmer. Keep the heat at a gentle simmer throughout, never a rolling boil. If the broth is already cloudy, you can strain it through a fine-mesh sieve or a muslin cloth.

items.symptom: Meat is still tough after 90 minutes
items.cause: Short ribs vary in thickness and the simmering temperature was too low
items.fix: Increase to a medium-low simmer and continue cooking. Some short rib cuts take up to 2.5 hours. The meat is ready when it pulls away from the bone easily with a gentle pull.

items.symptom: Broth tastes bland despite long cooking
items.cause: The ratio of water to ribs was too high, or not enough seasoning was added
items.fix: Taste the broth at the 1-hour mark. If it already tastes weak, remove the lid for the remainder of the cooking time to allow it to reduce and concentrate. Add the soy sauce and salt incrementally.

content.text: Galbitang has long been associated with important occasions in Korea. It appears at Chuseok and Lunar New Year and at family gatherings where the effort of the dish signals respect for the people being fed. At home, it is a weekend project rather than a weeknight dish. It is almost always served with rice, kimchi and a few simple banchan. The leftover broth is considered a prize.
